note: Coverage method changed this run, and it matters. A recursive rclone walk of the Aakara root returned 762 files today but 346 yesterday, with each listing containing files the other lacked -- including finished reel masters that a naive diff read as DELETED. They were not deleted: listing September/Reels and August/reels directly returned every one of them. A top-down -R walk under-reports non-deterministically even within a single root, so coverage is now established by an explicit breadth-first walk that lists every folder by its own id with retries (125 folders, 1,198 distinct files, 0 listing failures). That BFS was a strict superset of all five -R walks combined. Genuinely uncatalogued after this run: 18 files in the Aakara 'Hiral Goel' folder, now staged as IFM-540..547. CORRECTION to the 20 Sep entry: the 17 IMG_42xx/84xx files in Sakshi uploads and Certificates are NOT uncatalogued. That claim came from matching Drive ids, which misses copies. Matching by filename shows every one of them is already named in an existing row (IFM-484..500, 514, 527..532) as the backup frame of a moment whose lead frame is a neighbouring file in the same folder. No rows are owed for them, and the 'ignore IMG_42xx/IMG_84xx' filter in the task file is harmless after all -- it should still be deleted, but as tidying, not as a fix.

items.title: Two staged rows are invisible in the Library until a preview clip exists: IFM-542 (IMG_6602.MOV, 75MB -- Hiral leafing through the workbook) and IFM-547 (IMG_8010.MOV, 143MB -- the 12 Jun inflation session). Both have thumbnails and real Drive file links; they fail only the Video 'playable' half of the visibility rule. Needs scripts/ifm-make-previews.sh then media-audit.py, and both need a deploy first, so they light up on the second deploy.

IFM-545 is the smiling frame of the identical wall, outfit and pose as IFM-067, which is an existing rank-1 kit portrait with a closed-mouth expression. IFM-545 was deliberately held at rank 2 so the lead strip does not show the same backdrop twice, but the smiling frame may well be the better press lead. A human should look at the two side by side and decide which one leads.

Five 'IFM Internal_<Month>.pptx' decks (June, July, August, October) plus IFM_June Content.pptx and IFM_June Creatives.pptx are uncatalogued. These are Aakara's internal planning decks, not deliverables, so no rows were created. Worth a decision: catalogue them as planning documents, or add them to a permanent skip list so they stop surfacing here. Note there is an October Internal deck but no October Creatives deck yet.
